title: Leaving Benedict College after drinking with Pinckney's band
summary: White names the band's directors, then tells how Benedict's president told him to leave because he took a drink while playing with Tom Pinckney's band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Four years of age. Four years of age. Little Sammy Coates directed the band as a comedy director, however. Yes. Under me, under Hardy, under John Brown, and under Brooks Brockman. Brooks Brockman lived in Los Angeles until about three years ago, and he died. Now, I'm leaving the Jenkins orphanage now. I'm also leaving Benedict College. I didn't stay there, but a term and a half. The president told me the college could very well do without me next year for obvious reasons, some of which I hold as a secret that I know personally of myself. But Dr. Osmond, being the president, warned me that the college could not tolerate certain things. They were not too disgraceful for a young man to admit, but he just said that the college was too religious and couldn't stand this. That was that I would take a drink once in a while.
It's just the truth. How do college students drink now? Well, yes. Same as I don't know.

By me playing out with Pinkney and Johnson, Bill Johnson, the rest of them. Well, they said, come on, take a drink. It won't hurt you, boy. Well, I thought it was right to be obedient to those old men. Well, when I left the office, I ran away with the president's daughter, Dr. Jacksonville, when I got married by Dr. John E. Ford, Bethel Baptist Institutional Church in 1913. You want to cut it off for a minute?
